Accessible Rich Internet Applications (ARIA) & Roles ARIA attributes bridge accessibility gaps for complex interactive UI widgets (modals, accordions, tabs, dropdowns) where native HTML elements are insufficient. - `role="dialog"`: Identifies a modal container. - `aria-expanded="true|false"`: Communicates expand/collapse state of accordions or mobile drawer menus. - `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`: Provides accessible naming for icon-only buttons or search bars. - `aria-live="polite|assertive"`: Announces dynamic DOM content updates to screen readers without interrupting ongoing speech. ```html

`? Use `
` for self-contained, independently distributable content units (such as blog posts, user comments, or product cards). Generic `
` elements convey no semantic meaning to search engines or screen readers. ### Q2: What is the difference between `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby`? `aria-label` accepts a plain string value directly on the element. `aria-labelledby` takes one or more DOM element IDs whose text content provides the accessible label for the target control. ### Q3: Why is `alt` attribute required on `` tags? The `alt` attribute provides textual alternative descriptions for screen reader users and displays fallback text when image assets fail to load. For decorative images, use `alt=""` or `aria-hidden="true"`. ### Q4: How does semantic HTML improve SEO? Search engine web crawlers evaluate semantic tags (`
